transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sana Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (CTO, Acme Automotive), Priya Sharma (Platform Lead), Tom Wu (SRE)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to agree POC success criteria, workload sizing for benchmarking, and decide which deployment modes (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) to exercise during the POC. Customer is leaning towards Dedicated for predictability but is evaluating Hosted first for speed. Security/compliance requirements (retention, KMS, audit logs) push them to consider Private long-term.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency p50/p95 targets, cost per 1M tokens, throughput)
- Workload sizing and sample dataset for benchmarks
- Timeline and owners for sample data and benchmark runs
- Tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, Private (latency, cost, data residency, SSO/KMS)
- Next steps and follow-ups

Action items (recorded in notes above): see next_steps and action_items metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros?
[00:08] Mark (Acme): Hi, Mark here, CTO. We're evaluating options for embedding LLM capabilities into our diagnostics and customer support flows.
[00:15] Priya (Acme): Priya, Platform Lead, I'll be driving the POC from our side.
[00:19] Tom (Acme): Tom, SRE, I'll be on the infra side and running benchmarks with you.
[00:24] Jordan: Great. Sana, you're the SE, wanna set expectations for the call?
[00:29] Sana (Redwood SE): Yeah, thanks. Want to nail down success criteria, get an idea of your traffic and latency needs, and pick which deployment mode(s) to exercise. Also figure out logistics for sample data and benchmarking windows.

[00:48] Mark: High level, core success criteria are: p50 under 300ms for short queries, p95 under 1s for interactive flow, throughput of ~30 qps during peak for the customer support path. Cost target is more fuzzy but we want to see cost per 1M tokens under a threshold to justify production.

[01:20] Sana: Helpful. When you say "short queries" what's the typical input length?
[01:24] Mark: Mostly 32-128 tokens, sometimes up to 512 for debug dumps. The embeddings workload is separate, ~512 dims, batch size of 32 at low frequency.

[01:40] Tom: We also care about KV cache warmup for multi-step diagnostics — we expect some context caching to reduce latency.

[02:05] Jordan: Ok. On deployments: Hosted API gets you fastest time-to-value and Redwood handles ops. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and data isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) is what you'd pick for strict compliance or data residency.

[02:28] Mark: We're leaning Dedicated because we want predictable latency during business hours, but we want to try Hosted to move faster. Private is more of a longer-term requirement because of audit and KMS integration.

[02:47] Sana: Makes sense. For the POC we often run a two-phased approach: Phase 1 run on Hosted to validate model/quality and basic latency/cost; Phase 2 run on Dedicated to validate throughput and guaranteed SLOs and optional Private if audit requirements force it. That avoids long lead times.

[03:12] Priya: What about data handling? We need to ensure logs and transcripts don't persist beyond 30 days and must use our KMS for encryption at rest.
[03:22] Jordan: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can do envelope encryption and we have options for reduced retention and log redaction. We'll send the SOC2/ISO and network diagram.

[03:45] Tom: Is there an on-prem package or air-gapped? We have some teams that want air-gapped during the pilot.
[03:51] Sana: We do offer Private deployments for VPC and on-prem, but those take more lead time — usually several weeks to provision and test. For a pilot we recommend Hosted then Dedicated; Private would be next if needed.

[04:18] Mark: For benchmarking what do you need from us? Sample requests? Traffic profile?
[04:23] Sana: Ideally: (1) sample payloads representative of 80% of traffic, (2) target QPS and concurrency, (3) target input lengths and expected output lengths, (4) any prompt templates and temperature settings. Also a redaction spec for PII.

[04:45] Priya: We'll provide a daily traffic distribution, 7-day peak hour, sample payloads (anonymized), and the PII redaction rules. Can you also provide the benchmark harness?

[04:53] Sana: Yes, we'll provide the benchmarking harness and recommended client side settings (batching, timeouts). We'll also propose a small script to replay traffic.

[05:08] Jordan: For success criteria let's draft a short doc: p50/p95 latency targets, throughput numbers, quality metrics (e.g., pass rate on a set of 50 eval prompts), and cost per 1M tokens target.

[05:26] Mark: For quality, we need at least 90% pass rate on the top 50 prompts and no regression greater than 5% vs our internal baseline.

[05:37] Tom: On throughput, dedicated sizing: we're guessing ~2 x A100 equivalent for your loads?

[05:44] Sana: We'll size more precisely after we see sample traffic. Rough rule: if you want 30 qps at mean 100 tokens and low tail latency, you likely want a dedicated pool with multiple GPUs or use model variants or quantized instances. We'll propose configurations.

[06:05] Priya: How do fallbacks work? If Dedicated is saturated do you fail open to Hosted?

[06:11] Jordan: You can set routing policies — you can fall back to a cheaper model variant in the same pool or route to Hosted as overflow. We can set throttles and automatic fallback to maintain availability.

[06:32] Mark: Costwise, any ballpark differences?

[06:35] Sana: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; for low volume it can be cheaper. Dedicated has an upfront reserved commit but lowers unit cost at scale. Private adds platform fees and infra ops. We'll send a proforma with a few scenarios.

[06:55] Tom: We want to run at least two benchmark passes: one cold (KV cache cold) and one warm to see improvements. Can you simulate KV warm caching?

[07:03] Sana: Yes, our harness can do cold and warm runs. Note that caching behavior depends on sequence patterns; we'll capture both.

[07:18] Jordan: Logistics and timeline: if you can get sample data and traffic profile by 2026-06-14, we can schedule Hosted benchmark next week (target 2026-06-17), then Dedicated sizing and a Dedicated run the week after (2026-06-22). Private provisioning would be scoped in parallel but will likely be multi-week.

[07:40] Priya: That timeline sounds good. We'll circle back if any procurement approvals block us.

[07:48] Mark: A few questions on security: SSO integration, audit logs, and retention — can you integrate with our SAML?

[07:55] Jordan: Yes, SAML SSO is supported for both Hosted (via our managed console) and Dedicated/Private where you manage the control plane. Audit logs and per-request tracing can be exported to your SIEM for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has options to stream audit logs as well. We'll share docs.

[08:18] Tom: Any known limitations with quantized models for our use case? We've seen hallucinations degrade on 4-bit.

[08:24] Sana: There's a quality tradeoff; we include quantization profiles and recommended models per workload. For debug/diagnostic flows with factual consistency, we often recommend FP16 or lower quantization with evals to validate. We'll include quantization recommendations in the sizing doc.

[08:45] Mark: For the POC success doc — can you include pass/fail gates and owners? E.g., who approves quality?

[08:53] Jordan: Yes. Suggest owners: Acme product for quality sign-off (Mark), Acme infra for performance (Tom), Redwood for infra support (Sana/Jordan).

[09:05] Priya: Anything else on networking? We need egress rules and allowed IPs and an option for private peering if Dedicated.

[09:12] Sana: We'll send a network diagram and peering options. Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private supports full VPC control.

[09:25] Mark: Ok let's recap next steps.

[09:28] Jordan: Jordan: send pricing and sample SLA, SOC2/ISO packet, and Dedicated sizing guide by 2026-06-15.

[09:34] Sana: I'll schedule the benchmark and share the harness; need sample traffic by 2026-06-16 to hit the hosted run on 2026-06-17.

[09:41] Priya: We'll share sample data and redaction rules by 2026-06-14.

[09:45] Tom: We'll carve out time to join the benchmark window and validate results.

[09:50] Jordan: Great. Any final concerns?

[09:53] Mark: Only that if Private proves necessary we'll need a clear cost/ops breakout.

[09:58] Jordan: We'll include that in the proposal. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and docs.

[10:05] END
